Sediment

/SEH-duh-ment/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Sediment means solid matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid, or is deposited by water, wind, or ice.

When Theo poured the last of the homemade grape juice, a gritty layer of sediment slid out of the bottle and into his glass.

Worked Example

After the flood receded, a stripe of fine brown sediment marked how high the water had climbed up the barn wall.

The floodwater carried tiny solid particles, and when the water slowed and drained away, those particles settled out and were left behind on the wall. Solid matter that settles out of water (or is dropped by wind or ice) is sediment.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

deposit: matter laid down and left in place over time

residue: what remains behind after the rest is gone

silt: fine soil particles carried and dropped by water

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

froth: bubbles that rise to a liquid's surface

vapor: matter that rises into the air as gas or mist

Where it sits · how thick the settled layer is — film → sediment → sludge

film vs. sediment: A film is a whisper-thin coating; sediment is a genuine accumulated layer you can see and feel.

sludge vs. sediment: Sludge is heavier and thicker than sediment — a dense, oozy mass rather than settled particles.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — sedi-

Root — sedi-: to sit, settle (from sedere)

Suffix — -ment

Suffix — -ment: result or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Sedi- (from sedere, 'to sit, settle') + -ment ('result of') builds sediment — 'the result of settling': the solid matter that literally sits down at the bottom once the water goes still.

Use the root in a new word: reside

Use the root in a new word: reside: A family of owls resides in the hollow oak at the edge of the meadow.

Word Choice

Scientific / everyday

Sediment shows up in both kitchens (the grit at the bottom of juice or coffee) and geology class ('sedimentary rock' is built from ancient layers of it). Watch the sound-alike trap: sentiment — with an n — is a feeling, and has nothing to do with settling particles.
